problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a comprehensive waste-diversion strategy to lower the total volume of residual solid waste generated across several district processing centers. Initially, no diversion initiatives are in place.

The operational characteristics for each center are as follows:
* For Center A, the waste generation coefficient is 2.113, and the throughput is 139.76.
* For Center B, the waste generation coefficient is 3.0, and the throughput is 52.396.
* For Center C, the waste generation coefficient is 1.887, and the throughput is 84.134.
* For Center D, the waste generation coefficient is 1.724, and the throughput is 253.804.
* For Center E, the waste generation coefficient is 0.851, and the throughput is 290.957.
* For Center F, the waste generation coefficient is 1.286, and the throughput is 176.36.
* For Center G, the waste generation coefficient is 1.628, and the throughput is 173.742.
* For Center H, the waste generation coefficient is 0.634, and the throughput is 221.174.

To achieve diversion, several processing technologies can be implemented, each with a specific diversion rate:
* Technology 1 diverts 57% of the waste stream.
* Technology 2 diverts 23% of the waste stream.
* Technology 3 diverts 51% of the waste stream.
* Technology 4 diverts 83% of the waste stream.
* Technology 5 diverts 88% of the waste stream.
* Technology 6 diverts 29% of the waste stream.
* Technology 7 diverts 67% of the waste stream.
* Technology 8 diverts 68% of the waste stream.

Deploying a technology at a center incurs an incremental cost per unit of throughput. The cost matrix for all center–technology pairings is provided below:

| Center \ Technology | Tech1 | Tech2 | Tech3 | Tech4 | Tech5 | Tech6 | Tech7 | Tech8 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Center A | 112.146 | 41.96 | 96.891 | 151.078 | 155.525 | 114.448 | 31.51 | 31.699 |
| Center B | 157.271 | 166.424 | 79.704 | 166.296 | 17.906 | 146.606 | 113.807 | 198.057 |
| Center C | 29.459 | 167.713 | 152.756 | 66.565 | 199.869 | 95.449 | 76.23 | 165.178 |
| Center D | 93.423 | 198.852 | 157.37 | 55.02 | 164.034 | 121.706 | 76.62 | 145.043 |
| Center E | 130.226 | 41.537 | 36.455 | 49.258 | 49.319 | 21.278 | 76.655 | 63.406 |
| Center F | 112.366 | 71.494 | 143.77 | 64.973 | 60.795 | 173.023 | 197.243 | 139.067 |
| Center G | 28.093 | 192.927 | 159.281 | 184.566 | 198.572 | 174.739 | 34.109 | 174.555 |
| Center H | 57.439 | 145.165 | 167.412 | 154.68 | 138.485 | 102.997 | 119.711 | 61.056 |

The planning task is to determine which technologies to apply at each center (centers may adopt multiple technologies concurrently), and a center may also operate with partial diversion if required. The objective is to guarantee that the total residual waste volume is reduced by at least a proportion P = 0.407 of the baseline volume, while minimizing the aggregate implementation cost.
